parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a documented tier-1 government-facilities ban in this division and nationally funded settings with national passport/entry screening that can refuse on document discrepancy and invoke permanent fraud ineligibility, plus severe custody care denial. No presentation execution, police sweeps or visitor extortion are documented, private settings are not banned in the division, existing X passports remain valid and courts/enjoinments provide partial remedy. That scope and partial remedy keep it above severe targeting, but unremedied universal exposure plus entry and custody severity place it materially below 0.45-0.55 profiles.

entry_documents.exposure: National M/F-only passport processing; existing X valid to expiry. 2025 cable: refuse on sex-related document discrepancy/doubt and consider permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation; reports of passports confiscated/blocked and stranded travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist; civil-liberties suit and court challenges unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate to refusal, investigation, detention and birth-sex custody/facility placement; state bans do not pre-empt federal screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026: conversion-therapy model including short haircuts, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented operative visitor custody placement respecting identity or continuing medication; bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any entry, facility-trespass or immigration detention can move traveller into this custody regime; division debate raised solitary as 'reasonable accommodation', unresolved in statute.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division 2025 law, effective 1 July 2025, bars gender-identity bathrooms/locker/changing rooms in public schools, state colleges and state-owned buildings, including off-campus activities; national order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division bans are government-run facilities only, not all private buildings; 29 states nationally have no mapped ban, but that does not protect in this division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and division bans stack in schools, colleges, capitols and other government buildings; private hotels/shops are not documented as banned.

care_services.exposure: National policy directs removal of hormone medication in custody; emergency ward placement for visitors not documented; under-18 care bans and 2025-26 federal proposals documented mainly for residents.
care_services.protection: Division settled a health-contractor discrimination suit in 2024 with $300,000 and non-discrimination commitment; no documented visitor care shield.
care_services.interaction: Hospitalisation or detention can trigger both ward placement uncertainty and medication non-continuation; resident care bans do not directly prove visitor emergency denial.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National framing redefines sex at birth, removes gender-ideology materials, May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 66% poll support for birth-sex documents; division listed among worst legislative states. One trespass arrest for restroom use nationally, up to 60 days, 24h in men's ward.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented trans-presentation capital offence, police sweeps or visitor extortion; several executive orders blocked/enjoined and under litigation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises enforcement likelihood for facility and document rules; courts remain a partial check rather than a guarantee.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division school bathroom ban and 2021-22 female school-sports restrictions directly affect a travelling minor in schools/colleges; national orders direct investigation of schools/teachers facilitating social transition and describe minor care as mutilation.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented visitor minor exemption from school/facility rules; care orders are contested/enjoined in part.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent/guardian travelling with a minor faces school facility, sports and potential school-investigation exposure that an adult alone does not.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of anti-trans street violence, police sweeps or extortion against visitors in the dossier; public opinion shows support for restrictive document policy.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but division hate-crime law does not and division has no state anti-discrimination statute in employment/housing/public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If assaulted or detained, traveller relies on national backstop only in this division; absence of documented visitor violence is not proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility complaints in banned division have no documented working remedy; custody placement enforcement, hospital ward practice, border secondary screening frequency and X-marker acceptance at entry are incompletely documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active courts, passport litigation, enjoined orders, legal-aid FAQ and the 2024 health settlement show some functioning recourse, but not shown to reverse facility/entry/custody rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial court remedy does not cancel operative federal entry, facility and custody exposures unless pre-emption or reversal is documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: unremedied birth-sex public-facility rule enforced by staff/courts with no visitor exemption. This case is narrower - mainly government-owned facilities, not every public building - but adds entry fraud risk and custody hormone removal, so not materially safer.

Similar facilities ban upheld despite challenges, polite private sector, no presentation offence. This case rates lower: it adds national entry refusal/permanent-ineligibility screening and documented severe custody care denial, absent from that anchor's core.

Higher safety than this case. That profile has no presentation offence, facility restriction or birth-sex placement, and mediators secure readmissions/refunds. Here documented tier-1 facility exclusion, federal document screening and custody harm are operative.

Much higher safety. That profile has documented traditional acceptance, accepted foreign documents, identity-based facilities/wards and court compensation enforced. Here division law bans identity-based government facilities and national entry rules create discrepancy exposure.

parsed.synthesis: Operative interaction: foreign passport discrepancy can lead to refusal/fraud inquiry, then detention with hormone removal or birth-sex placement; in the division, any government school, college or state building triggers facility exclusion, and a minor adds school and sports rules. Private commerce, existing X validity, enjoined orders and active courts mitigate, but no documented remedy reverses the stacked federal-division exposures. Hence elevated-to-high risk, near 0.35-0.45, rated 0.38.
